correctness.rationale: The local product condition is equivalent to the third-edge conflict rule, since in a simple graph two witnesses at opposite endpoints cannot be the same edge unless they are the tested edge itself, which is excluded. All five states follow by conditioning on how many other selected edges meet the parent end of each child edge: when the parent edge is absent, zero selected children permits arbitrary absent-boundary states, one permits d+e at the chosen child and only a elsewhere, and at least two permits only a for unchosen and d for chosen. A present parent edge gives d or e under the same local restrictions. The leaf and root cases include the empty packing. For the arithmetic bound, a size-s child merged after p vertices has cost O((s+1)(p+1)); absorb p into sp (s>=1), charge sp to pairs whose LCA is the current vertex in distinct children, and charge s to descendant/ancestor incidences. This corrects the imprecise attribution of both linear terms in RESULT.md line 63. Subtree storage is O(n^2) coefficients and scalar specialization is O(n) operations, not bit bounds. The path and double-star examples also follow from their conflict graphs P3 plus P2 and K2,2 plus an isolated vertex, respectively. The proof, not the frozen test log, establishes the general claim.

value.rationale: Complete coefficient counts are worth computing, but the earlier record already supplies the same practical recurrence and the same per-child operations. The remaining gain is a useful implementation-analysis note: standard pair accounting replaces a global degree bound in the unchanged convolution algorithm. The frozen work delivers no faster method, intrinsic lower or bit bound, or additional invariant beyond what the known recurrence yields. That remainder does not justify a standalone new enumerator or a scientific repair.
